commands.review_summary:
The PR unifies LINE auto-reply batching so text, rich, and media messages use an available reply token together, moves quick replies to the final outgoing message, removes the obsolete reply-chunk helper, and adds recovery-focused coverage.

PR surface: Source -1, Tests +197. Total +196 across 8 files.

Reproducibility: yes. there is a high-confidence documented path: a genuine LINE inbound event with a reply token, text plus a Flex table, or six rich bubbles with quick replies. The supplied live proof predates the current base SHA, so this review treats the path as source-reproducible rather than independently re-run on current main.

target.title: fix(line): deliver rich replies on the reply token instead of the push quota
target.body: Closes #65656 Closes #109006 ## What Problem This Solves Ask a LINE bot on a free plan for something that comes back as a table, and once the account's monthly push quota is spent the explanation arrives but **the table silently does not**. Nothing tells the user anything is missing — they just get half an answer. The reporter's log line is `line final reply failed: HTTPFetchError: 429 -`, and their workaround was to ask the agent for raw Markdown so the table never became a Flex bubble at all. On paid plans the table still arrives, but as a detached second bubble that burns a quota message. The same batch also loses its quick reply buttons whenever a reply carries more than five rich bubbles: the buttons are attached to the fifth message, the sixth is pushed straight after, and LINE hides quick replies as soon as a newer message arrives. The offered actions are simply not there. ## Why This Change Was Made A LINE reply token carries up to five messages and costs nothing; push spends the account's monthly allowance. That is the entire reason this delivery path uses the batch APIs at all. But the path only put *text* on the token — the rich and media bubbles were handed to push afterwards: ```ts // before, extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.ts await deps.sendLineReplyChunks({ ... }); // text -> reply token await sendLineMessages(richMessages, false); // table/flex -> push -> 429 await sendLineMessages(mediaMessages, false); ``` So on a spent quota the table was pushed into a 429 and dropped, while four reply-token slots sat unused. Worth flagging for anyone reading the diff: the hard-coded `false` in those calls looks like the lever, but it isn't. `reply-chunks.ts` sets `replyTokenUsed = true` in its `catch` as well as on success, so by the time those lines run the reply branch inside `sendLineMessages` is already unreachable. Flipping `false` to `true` is a no-op — that is what #65673 did before it was closed. The token has to be shared *before* it is consumed, which means assembling one batch. Once text, rich and media are assembled into a single batch, the no-text branch below turns out to be doing the same thing already — same ordering, same `sendLineMessages(..., true)` call — so the two collapse into one path. That is where the second defect surfaced: the surviving branch capped the quick-reply carrier at the last reply-token slot: ```ts const targetIndex = replyToken && !replyTokenUsed ? Math.min(4, combined.length - 1) : combined.length - 1; ``` This is the only quick-reply attach site in the extension that caps the index — `outbound.ts:248` already uses the true last message — and per the LINE documentation buttons disappear when "Your LINE Official Account, the user, or a different member sends a new message in the room", so the trailing push wipes them. Collapsing the branches leaves one attach site with the same rule the push path already uses. Net result is **9 fewer lines than a fix for the table alone** would have needed (273 → 282 effective source lines, two defects), because the duplicated assembly is gone rather than doubled. ## User Impact - Replies that mix text with a table, Flex card, template, location or media now arrive **complete** on free-plan accounts with a spent push quota, instead of losing the bubble to a 429. - Those replies stop consuming push quota entirely when they fit in five messages, so the monthly allowance lasts longer for the proactive sends that actually need it. - Quick reply buttons now appear on replies carrying more than five bubbles. - No visible change otherwise: ordering is unchanged (text leads, or the bubbles lead when quick replies are present), and anything past the five-message limit still pushes as before. ## Evidence ### 1. Live LINE Messaging API, before vs after Both runs execute the real `deliverLineAutoReply` against a real LINE channel, driven by a genuine inbound webhook event with a real, signature-verified reply token, replying with the reporter's shape (explanatory text + a Markdown table). `totalUsage` is read from `GET /v2/bot/message/quota/consumption` immediately before and after each run. Identifiers redacted. **BEFORE — `main`** ``` [harness] real LINE event: signature=VALID replyToken=a2344c… POST /v2/bot/message/reply -> HTTP 200 messages: [text("Comparison of real estate investment:\n\nHo Chi Minh City leads on yield.")] POST /v2/bot/message/push -> HTTP 200 messages: [flex(altText="Table")] delivery status: delivered push quota totalUsage: before=11 after=12 DELTA=1 ``` The table goes out over push and spends a quota message. On an exhausted quota that call is the reporter's 429 and the table is gone. **AFTER — this PR** ``` [harness] real LINE event: signature=VALID replyToken=22bf80… POST /v2/bot/message/reply -> HTTP 200 messages: [text("Comparison of real estate investment:\n\nHo Chi Minh City leads on yield."), flex(altText="Table")] (no push call) delivery status: delivered push quota totalUsage: before=12 after=12 DELTA=0 ``` LINE returned two `sentMessages` ids for the single reply call — both bubbles delivered. **`DELTA=1` → `DELTA=0`**: the table no longer depends on push quota, so it can no longer be lost to a 429. | BEFORE — `main` (table pushed) | AFTER — this PR (table on the reply token) | |---|---| | | | Both renders are identical from the user's side, which is the point: the delivery route changed, the experience did not. ### 2. Live LINE Messaging API, quick reply placement Same harness, six numbered Flex bubbles plus `quickReplies: ["Alpha", "Beta"]` and no text, so the batch overflows the five-message reply limit. Observed on LINE for iOS (quick replies do not render on LINE for PC at all). **BEFORE — `main` rule `Math.min(4, …)`** ``` reply -> HTTP 200 [flex("Bubble 1"), flex("Bubble 2"), flex("Bubble 3"), flex("Bubble 4"), flex("Bubble 5") +QUICKREPLY] push -> HTTP 200 [flex("Bubble 6")] status: delivered ``` LINE for iOS: six bubbles arrive, **no Alpha/Beta buttons**. **AFTER — this PR** ``` reply -> HTTP 200 [flex("Bubble 1"), flex("Bubble 2"), flex("Bubble 3"), flex("Bubble 4"), flex("Bubble 5")] push -> HTTP 200 [flex("Bubble 6") +QUICKREPLY] status: delivered ``` LINE for iOS: six bubbles arrive, **Alpha/Beta buttons render above the input bar**. | BEFORE — `main` (no buttons) | AFTER — this PR (buttons render) | |---|---| | | | ### 3. Red/green Reverting only `auto-reply-delivery.ts` to `origin/main` (e5240b997e9) and keeping the tests: ``` × sends text and rich messages on one reply token instead of pushing the rich bubble × keeps an extracted markdown table on the reply token alongside text × keeps media on the reply token alongside text × pushes the whole bundled batch when the reply token call fails × keeps quick replies on the trailing bubble when the batch overflows the reply token × sends rich messages before quick-reply text so quick replies remain visible ✓ pushes only the messages that do not fit the reply token batch ✓ tags a later chunk failure after the reply batch without replaying delivered text ✓ uses reply token for rich-only payloads ✓ surfaces a visible partial delivery when an overflow bubble fails alongside quick-reply text ✓ surfaces a visible partial delivery when an overflow bubble fails after text without quick replies ✓ wraps a non-extensible rich failure without losing visible-send evidence ✓ falls back to push when reply token delivery fails ✓ honors channelData.line.mediaKind on the reply-token path instead of forcing image … (18 passed) Tests 6 failed | 18 passed (24) ``` With the fix applied: ``` Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 24 passed (24) ``` The five-or-fewer-bubbles case is covered on both sides of the quick-reply change (`uses reply token for rich-only payloads` stays green throughout — that rule is unchanged below the limit). ### 4. Full checks ``` $ vitest run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-line.config.ts extensions/line/src Test Files 28 passed (28) Tests 361 passed | 1 skipped (362) $ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.extensions.json --noEmit -> exit 0 $ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/line -> exit 0 $ oxfmt --check extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.ts extensions/line/src/auto-reply-delivery.test.ts All matched files use the correct format. $ node scripts/check-deadcode-exports.mjs -> exit 0 ``` (`bot-message-context.test.ts` is excluded from the suite line above: it fails on this machine before any change, because Node 22.16 ships SQLite 3.49.1 and OpenClaw requires 3.51.3+. Unrelated to this diff.) ### 5. What was not tested - **The 429 itself.** The account's push quota was not exhausted, so no live `429` was observed. The quota-consumption delta is the proxy: `DELTA=1` means the table depends on the push allowance and therefore inherits its 429; `DELTA=0` means it no longer touches that allowance at all. The reporter's log supplies the 429 half. - **LINE for Android.** Quick replies were verified on LINE for iOS only. LINE for PC renders no quick replies at all, so it cannot exercise that path. - **Overflow beyond ten messages.** The push batching loop (`for (let i = 0; i < messages.length; i += 5)`) is unchanged by this PR and already covered. ### 6. References - LINE — reply API carries up to five messages, quota-free: https://developers.line.biz/en/reference/messaging-api/#send-reply-message - LINE — rate limits and push quota: https://developers.line.biz/en/reference/messaging-api/#rate-limits - LINE — quick reply support and disappearance rules: https://developers.line.biz/en/docs/messaging-api/using-quick-reply/
